summary: Iteration 7: E2E verification of Request-Changes + Approval-Record feature. Backend pytest (4/4 pass): 401 without token, 422 on empty note, 409 on final_delivered (May Recap), seed sanity. Frontend Playwright end-to-end (all 7 steps pass): Q3 Teaser opened fresh 0/2 → request changes round 1 with timecode 00:10 → toast 'round 1 of 2 included' → chip 1/2, status REVISIONS REQUESTED, request-changes-btn hidden, approve-cut-btn visible → approve → status APPROVED with approval-record 'Approved by Demo Client · Aug 5, 2026', request-changes-btn reappears → round 2 → chip 2/2 amber (bg-warn/15 text-warn), toast 'round 2 of 2 included' → approve again → open request-changes 3rd time → extra-round-warning banner IS visible ('Heads up: all 2 included revision rounds are used...') → submit → WARNING toast 'Revision round 3 exceeds the 2 included rounds — this round may be billed as an extra' → chip 3/2. Admin view: demo client selected, Q3 Teaser row shows 'revisions 3/2' with admin-extra-rounds-badge-0 reading '1 extra round — billable'. admin-deliv-rounds input present; created 'TEST_Rounds Deliverable' linked to a booking with rounds=1, row shows 'revisions 0/1'. Newly-created row tagged is_seed_data=true via service key for cleanup.
critical_code_review_comments: DeliverableDetail.js request-changes-btn is visible for statuses in_review AND approved but not for revisions_requested — correct per spec. However there is no visible feedback about *why* the button disappears mid-flow; a small caption 'awaiting new cut from studio' next to the chip while status=revisions_requested would improve UX.

The approve endpoint clears approved_by_* on request_changes (good) but sets approved_at=None only on request_changes — if an admin manually PATCHes status back to in_review via /api/admin/deliverables/{id}, approved_by fields are not cleared, so a stale 'Approved by X' banner could appear. Consider centralising the reset in a DB trigger on status change.

server.py request_changes uses (d.get('revision_rounds_used') or 0) + 1 which is safe, but the underlying column has default 2 (per problem statement 'included_revision_rounds default 2') — verify revision_rounds_used default is 0 (confirmed via seed check: all 0). OK.

Frontend chip amber styling triggers at roundsUsed >= roundsIncluded which correctly flips at 2/2 and 3/2. Chip becomes red-adjacent (warn tone) but there's no strictly 'over-budget' variant to distinguish 3/2 vs 2/2 visually. Consider a separate 'exceeded' color once used>included.
Sonner toast for extra round uses toast.warning which renders as yellow — visually identical to chip color; consider toast.error for stronger signal on billable rounds.
